title: I Faked Receiving A Threatening Letter to The Editor of this "Journal"
subtitle: Not to be left out, I made up a threatening letter to myself.
body_html:
There's been difficult letters going around to academic journals. There were years, before this one, when being the editor of a highly technical journal like CHEST—an academic publication dedicated to highly political topics like pneumonia, pneumothorax, and other pathology of the part of the body right below the neck and above the abdomen—was a great way to stay out of the limelight. However, they've been getting letters from the government asking them to include other perspectives. Like for example, where are all the articles about feet? These are the questions we demand the editors of journals like CHEST to answer.

I can imagine the editor of CHEST, on an unsuccessful date, trying to explain that it's not actually a pornographic magazine, it's a peer reviewed publication! Those were the good old days.

Today, I am going to pretend that this publication got a threatening letter also, from a nefarious source, as a way to garner publicity, no matter how unwarranted, for my backwater of a newsletter. Ladies and gentlemen, humans of all shapes and sizes, I share with you, a completely falsified threatening letter that I absolutely didn't receive this week, but I'm going to pretend that I did.

Share

As United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, I receive frequent requests for information and clarification. I don't receive many invitations to fashionable parties, much less invitations to the reopening of the Brooklyn Mirage. Given my frustration, I am forced to live a life where I take these requests— those very important request for information and clarification, that people casually send United States Attorneys Office, seriously. Given my lack of exciting evenings, which is particularly troubling given the fact that I live in the very exciting city of New York, or at least it’s exciting for other people, I am left with nothing to do but act on request for information and clarification. How do I respond to such requests for information and clarification? Get ready for it.

Are you ready for it?

I said are you ready?

That's right, with letters like this one. It has been brought to my attention that more and more journals and publications like The Frontier Psychiatrists are conceding that they are partisans in various debates!

Just the other day, I saw you, this very newsletter, when I casually checked, write a parody poem about a regulatory or policy issue. You had a very specific point of view, didn't you? Did you think about what other perspectives you could offer? Did you even bother to imagine writing such an article in iambic pentameter?

Admit it, as a health themed satire publication, your perspectives are in a certain direction. That is, that they have a position for which they are advocating either due to an attempt to garner advertisement (under postal code) or sponsorship (under relevant fraud regulations). It seems like you're trying to be funny. You know what I didn't think it was? You're never gonna guess. Just come on, guess. Guess what I'm thinking! Come on, nobody ever guesses!

The public has certain expectations and you have certain responsibilities.

Would you please answer these questions:

  • ﻿﻿How do you assess your responsibilities to protect the public from viciously accurate information about the actual state of healthcare in America, much less health insurance, and how loathsome and deplorable the process of trying to attain healthcare can be?

  • ﻿﻿How do you clearly articulate to the public when you have certain viewpoints that are influenced by your ongoing relations with other Substack writers, like for example, who has been accused of being critical of psychiatry? We've even heard you are in the process of reviewing a book, a critical book, with a perspective, and yet haven't gotten the review done yet, despite having a copy of the book for some time? Do you have a link to the book? We'd like to send Dr Aftab a threatening letter in the routine course of our Affairs.

  • ﻿﻿Do you accept articles or essays from competing viewpoints— serious viewpoints? People who don't try to be funny. People who are just telling it like it is? People who are struggling to find a link to Dr Aftab’s book?

  • This is an Amazon affiliate link to Awais Aftab’s book. Now, stop complaining.

  • ﻿﻿How do you assess the role played by government officials and funding organizations like the National Institutes of Health, judging by the fact that they don't fund humorous articles? Do you think I'm trying to be funny now? I'm super cereal.

  • ﻿﻿How do you handle allegations that authors of works in your newsletter may have mildly amused readers?

  • If you're going to the Mirage, can I come?

  • If you're not going to the Mirage, can I have your ticket?

  • Look, I've never been to the Mirage, and there are rumors circulating, rumors that have been sent to my office, by concerning citizens, that you have a ticket. Hook an attorney up, bro.

I am also interested to know if publishers, journals, and organizations with which you work are adjusting their method of acceptance of competing viewpoints. Maybe United Healthcare is not so bad? Maybe pharmacy benefit managers are doing a great job? Are there new jokes being developed and offered? How about different sassy takes on Health and its care, but focusing on the exciting changes happening as value is being returned to shareholders? Maybe, Dr. Muir, psychiatric drugs are a good enough answer?

I look forward getting an invitation to go to the Mirage, or even the House of Yes, and appreciate your cooperation with my letter of inquiry. Please respond by May 6, 2025. Yes, I know that's your birthday. I know a lot of things. Should you have further questions regarding this matter, please do not hesitate to call my office or schedule a time to meet in person. I bet you can figure out what venue I would suggest. Let me suggest…some time between 11 PM and 11:59 PM, on Saturday?

All the best,

A disgruntled US Attorney.

I swear to God not a single word of that above letter was made up. It is all completely true.

I'm shaking in my boots. Oh, sorry, that's just the bass from these new speakers here at the Brooklyn Mirage! Just hanging there, for reasons unclear, with my children.
